title: Constructing the FAST S-Box Pool Generator
summary: FAST allows each S-box to be any permutation of its alphabet, but determining or constructing the pseudorandom generator for the S-box pool remains open.

formal_statement.body: The Sbox-generation step maps an $L^2$-bit key $K_S$ to an Sbox pool $S$ using $\mathrm{PRNG}_{2,a,m}(K_S)$, where each Sbox may be any permutation of $\mathbb{Z}_a$. The unresolved task is to determine or construct the $\mathrm{PRNG}_{2,a,m}$ used for this generation; the choice of this generator remains open.

scope.domain: S-box-pool generation for the FAST format-preserving encryption and tokenization design.
parameters: L: key-length parameter, with K_S containing L squared bits
K_S: key input to the S-box-pool generator
a: defines the set Z_a, whose permutations may serve as S-boxes
m: parameter of the S-box-pool generator
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine or construct the generator PRNG2,a,m for the S-box-generation step.

citations.label: FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization

progress.summary: The paper explicitly says that the choice of PRNG2,a,m is open and follows this statement with a suggested Fisher–Yates implementation.
citation_labels: F. Betül Durak et al., FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization
